elements.text: If sudden nausea/vomiting and any of: generalised itch/rash, face/tongue swelling, wheeze, difficulty breathing, BP < 90/60, dizziness/collapse or exposure to possible allergen2, check for anaphylaxis 28

elements.text: Neck stiffness, drowsy/confused or purple/red rash: meningitis likely

elements.text: Shock1/SBP < 80

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with nausea/vomiting and any of:
elements.text: Vomiting blood
Manage and refer urgently:
If shock, SBP < 80 or pancreatitis likely, give sodium chloride 0.9% 500mL IV over 30 minutes, repeat until systolic BP > 80. Continue 1L 6 hourly. Stop if breathing worsens.
If meningitis likely, give ceftriaxone 2g IV3/IM. Avoid injecting > 1g IM at one injection site.

If pain severe, give morphine 5-10mg IM, repeat 4-6 hourly until patient referred, or give diluted morphine4 3-10mg slow IV: start with 3mL IV over 3 minutes. If needed, give another 1mL/ minute until pain improved, up to 10mL. Stop if BP < 90/60.
Check fingerprick glucose. If glucose < 3 (< 4 if diabetes) or ≥ 11.1 19.
NAUSEA/VOMITING

Yes Gastroenteritis likely • If nausea/vomiting, give metoclopramide 10mg 8 hourly as needed for up to 5 days. • Give oral rehydration solution. • If diarrhoea, give loperamide 4mg initially, then 2mg after each loose stool if needed, up to maximum dose per weight6. • If abdominal cramps are distressing, give hyoscine butylbromide 10mg 6 hourly for up to 3 days. • Advise patient to drink lots of fluids, eat small frequent meals as able and avoid fatty food. • Advise patient to return if symptoms worsen, vomiting > 3 days or not tolerating oral fluids.

Approach to the patient with nausea/vomiting not needing urgent attention • If thirst, dry mouth or poor skin turgor, dehydration likely, give single dose metoclopramide 10mg orally/IM/IV. Then give oral rehydration solution and observe: encourage small frequent sips. Aim for 1-2L in first 2 hours. If vomits, wait 10 minutes and try again more slowly. • If unable to drink or no better after 2 hours, give sodium chloride 0.9% 500mL IV over 30 minutes and refer. • Exclude pregnancy 174. If pregnant, reassure that nausea/vomiting is common in first trimester. Encourage to eat smaller meals more frequently and drink fluids regularly. • If associated dizziness 46. • Review medication: NSAIDs (e.g. ibuprofen), metformin, contraceptives, hormone therapy, chemotherapy and morphine can cause nausea/vomiting. Discuss with doctor. If on DS-TB medication 108, RR-TB medication 117 or ART 131. • Screen for alcohol/drug use: in the past year, has patient: drunk ≥ 4 drinks5/session, used illegal drugs or misused prescription or over-the-counter medications? If yes to any 165.
Is there recent onset vomiting with cramping abdominal pain, diarrhoea, loss of appetite, body pain or fever?
No • Assess for stress and anxiety 98. • If patient has a life limiting illness, give palliative care 191. • Discuss/refer if: - Nausea/vomiting
persists > 2 weeks. - Uncertain of diagnosis.

Yes. Dyspepsia (heartburn) likely • Advise to stop NSAIDS (e.g. ibuprofen/aspirin). If smoking, encourage to stop 164. Avoid fizzy drinks, fatty/ late night meals. • Limit alcohol/caffeine/spicy food. Eat small frequent meals. Sleep on left side with upper body elevated. • If BMI ≥ 25 and waist circumference ≥ 80cm (woman) or ≥ 94cm (man), gastro-oesophageal reflux disease likely. Assess and manage overweight/obesity 156. • Discuss/refer if any of: Hb < 12 (woman) or < 13 (man), blood in vomit or black, sticky, tar-like stool (melaena), difficulty or pain with swallowing, persistent vomiting, unintentional weight loss, recurrent symptoms with: > 50 years, history of previous gastric surgery, family history of stomach/oesophageal cancer. • Give omeprazole 20mg daily for 14 days. Avoid if on atazanavir/ritonavir. Discuss with specialist. • Advise to return if no better after 7 days. Refer.
